videos.title: Enthalpy, Entropy and Non-Equilibrium Reactions | Year 12 Chemistry
videos.description:
Explain why burning glucose and photosynthesis stay away from equilibrium, using the signs of the enthalpy change and the entropy change. Read the sign of the Gibbs free energy change (delta G) to decide whether a reaction is favoured, and keep that separate from how fast it runs. Work through the glucose example one step at a time, then compare the reverse process, photosynthesis.

Chemistry 2017: Year 12 Module 5, Equilibrium and Acid Reactions. Supports analysing non-equilibrium systems in terms of the effect of entropy and enthalpy.
Syllabus dotpoint (NSW Chemistry Stage 6, 2017, Module 5):
"analyse examples of non-equilibrium systems in terms of the effect of entropy and enthalpy, for example:
- combustion reactions
- photosynthesis"
Official 2017 course: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/chemistry-stage-6-2017

Prerequisite: Dynamic equilibrium in a closed system, exothermic and endothermic reactions, entropy as the spread of particles and energy, and the link between enthalpy, entropy and delta G. Next: What a flask already at equilibrium does when it is disturbed by a change in concentration or temperature.

videos.title: Squeezing a Gas Equilibrium: Predicting the Shift | Year 12 Chemistry
videos.description:
Squeeze a gas mixture that is sitting at equilibrium and predict which way it shifts by counting only the gas particles. Explain the shift as the side with fewer gas particles becoming favoured when every gas is more crowded. Handle equal gas counts and solids, and tell a squeeze apart from adding an inert gas at fixed volume.

Chemistry 2017: Year 12 Module 5, Equilibrium and Acid Reactions. Supports explaining how pressure and volume changes affect an equilibrium, using Le Chatelier’s principle and collision theory.
Syllabus dotpoint (NSW Chemistry Stage 6, 2017, Module 5):
"investigate the effects of temperature, concentration, volume and/or pressure on a system at equilibrium and explain how Le Chatelier’s principle can be used to predict such effects"
"explain the overall observations about equilibrium in terms of the collision theory"
Official 2017 course: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/chemistry-stage-6-2017

Prerequisite: Le Chatelier’s principle for concentration and temperature changes, why a disturbance is only partly cancelled, and gas pressure as particles hitting the walls (Year 11). Next: Catalysts and equilibrium, a faster route to the same mixture.

#Year12Chemistry #Equilibrium #HSCScience

videos.title: How DNA Is Copied: Base Pairing and Replication | Year 12 Biology
videos.description:
Explain how a cell copies billions of DNA letters almost without error. Name the parts of a DNA nucleotide, pair A with T and C with G, and explain why one strand acts as a template for the other. Trace a short molecule through semi-conservative replication, where each new molecule keeps one original strand, and explain why copying errors are rare.

Biology 2017: Year 12 Module 5, Heredity. Supports modelling DNA replication using the Watson and Crick model, including nucleotide composition, pairing and bonding.
Syllabus dotpoint (NSW Biology Stage 6, 2017, Module 5):
"model the processes involved in cell replication, including but not limited to:
- DNA replication using the Watson and Crick DNA model, including nucleotide composition, pairing and bonding"
Official 2017 course: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/biology-stage-6-2017

Prerequisite: DNA as inherited information, genes, alleles and copying errors, and how a single cell copies its DNA before it splits. Next: Mitosis, how a cell shares its copied chromosomes between two new cells.

#Year12Biology #DNA #HSCScience
